1. AB higher-a (A/B implementation test): analysis denominator eligible participants randomized to each design; target 152 per design (304 in total), shown by Research Studio as 304; recruit about 380.

1. AB higher-a (A/B implementation test)
Primary analysis: compare the alternative with Design A (Current flow), the control, on task success (success signal). Each design's denominator is every eligible participant randomized to it. Anyone randomized who drops out or whose success cannot be measured counts as not successful; nobody is removed after randomization. People screened out or lost to technical failures before randomization are in no denominator.
Report each design's rate with a 95% Wilson score interval and the difference from the control with a two-sided Newcombe hybrid score interval at 95%. An interval that excludes zero is reported as a clear difference; an interval that includes zero is reported as inconclusive, not as evidence that the designs perform the same. No winner is declared automatically: the team judges whether a difference matters in practice.
Target sample (estimate): 152 randomized eligible participants per design (304 in total) to detect a change from 60% to 75% with 80% power. Recruit about 380 (304 ÷ (1 − 0.20)), allowing for 20% of recruits not reaching the analysis (screen-outs, ineligible people and technical failures before randomization).
Stopping rule: Analyse once after both designs reach the target.
Before interpreting outcomes, check: group sizes (sample-ratio check), drop-out by design, success-tracking coverage by design and device mix. Any problem is reported with the results.
Secondary measures (success among finishers with success measured; self-reported completion; active time on task; drop-out by design) are reported descriptively with intervals for context and are not used to decide between designs.

plan.analysis:
Sample size and recruitment
Loss assumption: 20% of recruits won't reach each activity's analysis denominator, so each target is recruited as n ÷ (1 − 0.20).
Research Studio's sample-size summary and size text show each analysis target "plus extra for drop-out"; the recruit numbers here already include that extra.
Research Studio's size text calls prototype-task, tree-test and first-click targets "people completing the activity": read them as people who start, as its standard analysis does.
1. prototype discover (Prototype usability): analysis denominator people completing a usable session, per round; target 5 per round (15 in total), shown by Research Studio as 15; recruit about 7 per round (21 in total).
2. card_sort explore (Card sorting): analysis denominator completed sorts; target 20; recruit about 25.
3. tree_test tree (Tree testing): analysis denominator people who start the activity; target 81; recruit about 102.
4. survey survey (Survey): analysis denominator completed responses; target 97; recruit about 122.

1. prototype discover (Prototype usability)
List usability problems from click histories and follow-up answers, with the number of participants who met each and its severity. Counts describe this sample and are not population rates. Report self-reported completion and time for context.
Analysis denominator: people who complete a usable session in each round.

2. card_sort explore (Card sorting)
Use completed sorts. Report the similarity matrix (share of participants who grouped each pair together), common group names and cards with no clear home (no partner grouped with it by at least 60% of participants). Group names are not merged automatically.
Analysis denominator: completed sorts.

3. tree_test tree (Tree testing)
Report task success (ended at a correct destination) with a 95% Wilson interval, directness (no backtracking), first-level choices and the most common wrong destinations. People who started the activity but did not finish count as not successful. Compare with the benchmark of 70%: above if the whole 95% interval is above it, below if the whole interval is below it, otherwise inconclusive.
Analysis denominator: everyone who starts the activity; anyone who starts but doesn't finish stays in it and counts as not successful.

4. survey survey (Survey)
Summarise each question: distribution and median for scales, counts and percentages with 95% intervals for choices, and themes for open text.
Analysis denominator: completed responses.

texts.text: 5 people per round, 3 rounds (15 in total), fixing problems between rounds. Small rounds find many of the most common problems; problems few people meet need more participants. Results describe problems, not rates for the whole population.
About 20 people completing the sort. For open card sorts, 15–30 is common practice; similarity scores tend to settle at around 15–20 participants (Tullis & Wood, 2004).

About 81 people completing the activity, so that task success (correct destination) near 70% is estimated to within about ±10 points (95% interval). Many teams recruit about 50 per tree. Recruit extra for drop-out.
About 97 people completing the activity, so that a percentage answer near 50% is estimated to within about ±10 points (95% interval). Recruit extra for drop-out.
